Recent work separates sampling allocation, loss scale, and gradient interaction. [PiKE (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.06244) adapts task sampling using positive gradient interactions; its low-conflict findings concern large-scale pretraining, not established BERT4Rec behavior. [Dual-Balancing (2025)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41289618/) treats loss-scale balancing and gradient-magnitude balancing separately. [Sparse Training (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18615) studies updating parameter subsets to reduce conflict; this does not establish that sparse diagnostic measurements accurately estimate full-network conflict.

For the proposed audit, public literature cannot resolve the local fixed-branch versus Bernoulli documentation conflict. Proposed evidence: checkpoint-linked source/configuration hashes, sampler mode and probabilities, RNG states, realized branch counts, selected-target counts, loss numerators/denominators, and applied coefficients. For pooled target normalization, L=Σ_b S_b/Σ_b n_b; for separately normalized branches, L=Σ_b λ_b S_b/n_b. These imply different supervision weights when target counts vary. Fixed quotas and Bernoulli allocation can match expected counts while differing in variance; exact accounting must include empty-branch handling and any probability correction.

Recommended controls: hold sampled contexts and masks fixed while changing normalization; hold normalization fixed while changing allocation; then vary context construction with matched allocation and target counts. At selected checkpoints, measure branch gradients on paired batches, separately for item embeddings and encoder: norms, dot products, cosine/conflict frequency, and centered covariance across repeated draws. Report probe counts, uncertainty, zero-gradient handling, and sampled-coordinate coverage; distinguish covariance from uncentered gradient alignment. These are proposed controls, not observed findings. Keep probes within each category’s single BERT4Rec network and retain the pinned validation evaluator.
